SPREADSHEET/CLIPBOARD SINK: fuzzed 24 sneaky leading characters (​ ‎ ﻿ ­ ᠎     lone \uD800   　   − ＝ ‐  ؜ ⁦ ' " \ TAB CR LF ) x 5 formula payloads (=1+1, +1, -1, @SUM(1), =cmd|'/C calc'!A0) through BOTH name authorities, then asserted no resulting cell begins with =,+,-,@ after splitting the CSV on any of , ; TAB LF and after the same split on the clipboard line. 36 distinct survivor names, 0 violations. saturationDecisions.why: at gate (3) but a changed path is on its surface
at gate (3) but a changed path is on its surface

themes.theme: App.tsx keeps three independent, hand-copied slices of dispatch-time state (names, settings, constraintRows); reroll only re-commits two of them, so the setup dialog can reopen showing rules from an abandoned edit next to the roster actually on screen.
findingSummaries: `handleReroll` re-commits `names` and `settings` from the view but deliberately leaves `constraintRows` untouched, so after an abandoned Edit→Generate the reopened roster editor shows the view's roster next to the abandoned edit's buddy rules — and pressing Generate silently applies rules that were never in force on the graph on screen.
themes.remediation: Eliminate the third independently-written copy instead of adding a reminder to update it: carry the typed rule rows on `GraphView` itself (alongside `constraints`) so `viewFromResult`/`loadView` produce them and every dispatch-time consumer, including reroll, reads rows from the one view object rather than a parallel `constraintRows` slot in App state. Do not rebuild rows from `view.constraints` via `toNamedPairs` — that reintroduces the silent-row-deletion defect already fixed in round 15.

themes.theme: Live-region elements exist for key async/state-changing actions (clipboard copy, roster generation) but are left empty or merely cleared on completion, so keyboard/screen-reader users get no announced outcome — success, failure, or otherwise.
findingSummaries: BuddyList's Copy button awaits copyText() and only handles the ok===true branch; when the clipboard write rejects, copyAll() does nothing observable — no label change, no live-region text, no toast — leaving a screen-reader user with no signal the export failed or that CSV/Export exist as an alternative.

On successful generate/reroll, the only live-region change is `.busy-live` going from "Generating…" to "" — an emptying that most screen readers announce as nothing — while `.sr-live` stays empty too, so the sole accessible cue that the graph exists is an incidental focus move into an empty search box rather than any stated result.
themes.remediation: Stop treating 'clear the live region' as the terminal state for these two flows: in both `copyAll()` and the generate/reroll completion handler, replace the empty-string end state with a short outcome sentence written into the existing live region (failure message for copy, result summary for generate) using the same region and commit pattern already in place — do not introduce new live-region elements or a shared announcement abstraction.

themes.theme: A blob-backed download can be silently dropped because the object URL is revoked in the same synchronous task as the click that consumes it, on an anchor never attached to the document.
findingSummaries: `downloadBlob` calls `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` synchronously right after `a.click()`, on an anchor that is never attached to the document — either condition alone can cause a browser to drop the download silently, with no error surfaced, and both are present here.
themes.remediation: In the one shared `downloadBlob` helper, attach the anchor before clicking and defer the revoke to a later task: `document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); a.remove(); setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 0);` — no new helper, just correcting the existing single call site that all export sinks already share.

gating.theme: the setup dialog can be opened showing state from two different generation attempts, because only two of App's three dispatch-time copies are re-committed by a reroll
gating.summary: `handleReroll` re-commits `names` and `settings` from the view but deliberately leaves `constraintRows` untouched, so after an abandoned Edit→Generate the reopened roster editor shows the view's roster next to the abandoned edit's buddy rules — and pressing Generate silently applies rules that were never in force on the graph on screen.
gating.failure:
Reproduced in `.review-scratch/rc/appRules.test.tsx` and `appRules2.test.tsx` (App + stubbed worker). (1) Generate roster `Alice..Fay` with no rules → view A. (2) Edit people → roster `Zed..Uma`, add rule `Zed`/`Yan`, Generate, then cancel (status→idle; view is still A). (3) Click "Different arrangement" — the dispatch carries `{required:[],prohibited:[]}` and `names`/`settings` are re-committed to A. (4) Click "Edit people": the roster textarea correctly reads `Alice
Bob
Carol
Dan
Eve
Fay`, but the disclosure reads "Buddy rules (1)" and Rule 1 is `Zed`/`Yan`, flagged unknown — a rule count for a graph that has none. Second variant: with the abandoned edit's rule naming two people who ARE in roster A (`Alice`/`Bob`, kind `prohibited`), the reopened editor shows roster A plus that rule, and the very next Generate dispatches `constraints: {required: [], prohibited: [[0,1]]}` — a constraint the user never applied to this roster. App.tsx's own comment at the RosterModal call site ("All three RosterModal inputs are DISPATCH-time") is false after any reroll. This is the unfixed sibling of the `names` bug closed in round 15 and the `settings`/seed bug closed in round 13; the existing suite pins both of those and nothing pins the rows across a reroll.
gating.remediation: Close the theme rather than the case: make the rule rows travel with the roster they were submitted against instead of living in a separate, independently-written state. Either carry the typed `NamedPair[]` on `GraphView` (alongside `constraints`, so `viewFromResult` and `loadView` both produce it and an adopted view carries its own rows), or have `handleReroll` write `constraintRows` from the same source it writes `names` from. The second is a one-line addition but re-creates the "remember to write all three" instruction that already failed twice here; the first removes the third copy entirely, which is the subtraction the two earlier fixes were each half of. Do NOT rebuild rows from `view.constraints` via `toNamedPairs` — that is the silent-row-deletion defect closed in round 15.
gating.invariant: Whenever RosterModal is opened with a roster text equal to `view.names.join("\n")`, resolving the rule rows it is opened with against that roster (`resolveNamedPairs(rows, view.names).pairs`) must equal `view.constraints` exactly. More generally: no App state transition may write `names` from one origin and leave `constraintRows` describing a different origin — the roster text, the settings and the rule rows handed to RosterModal always describe one and the same submission or adopted view.

gating.theme: an action that can fail produces literally nothing observable when it does — a keyboard/screen-reader user cannot distinguish "it worked" from "nothing happened" from "it's still running"
gating.summary: BuddyList's Copy button awaits copyText() and only handles the ok===true branch; when navigator.clipboard.writeText rejects (permission denied, insecure context, no Clipboard API, focus-not-in-document at write time, etc.) copyText() resolves false and copyAll() does nothing at all — no button-label change, no live-region text, no toast. Reproduced with a scratch test (app/.review-scratch/copyfail.test.tsx, mocking copyText to resolve false): after the click and a settle, the button's chipbtn text is still "Copy" and the .sr-live region is still "". A screen-reader user who presses Copy in this state hears and sees nothing whatsoever, and has no way to know the export failed or that CSV/Export exist as an alternative — this is precisely the 'recover from an error along the way' step in the task scenario, and there is no recovery surface at all.
gating.failure: Mock copyText() to resolve false (as it legitimately does on any clipboard-write failure/rejection) and click the Copy button in BuddyList: the chipbtn label stays "Copy" and the adjacent role="status" region's textContent stays "" — confirmed by running the reproduction script (see below) against the real component.
gating.remediation: Add an else branch in copyAll() (app/src/panels/BuddyList.tsx:47) that surfaces a failure the same way the success path does — e.g. set the `announced` live-region text to a message like "Couldn't copy — try CSV instead" (and optionally a transient error class on the button), following the same empty-then-refill two-commit pattern already used for the success announcement so it is reliably re-announced on a repeated failed press too.
gating.invariant: For every resolution of copyText() (true or false), copyAll() must produce a DOM mutation in a live region or focused control that is observably different depending on the outcome — i.e. the accessible-text state after a failed copy must differ from both the pre-press state and the successful-copy state.

gating.theme: a major, page-replacing state transition (roster submitted -> graph ready) has no textual live-region announcement of its own outcome; the only accessible signal is an implicit focus move into an unrelated, empty control
gating.summary: On a successful generate/reroll, the only live-region change is `.busy-live` going from "Generating…" to "" (App.tsx:438) — an emptying, which most screen readers either do not announce or announce as nothing useful. Neither `.sr-live` region (path status, selection status) gains text at this transition, since nothing is selected and no path is active yet. The sole accessible cue that the graph exists is `useFocusRescue` moving focus into the (empty) "Find a person" search box once the busy overlay's Cancel button is removed from the DOM. Reproduced with a scratch test (app/.review-scratch tree) dumping every `[aria-live]` region's textContent immediately before and after the running->done transition: busy-live is the only element whose content differs, and it differs by becoming empty, not by stating a result. A screen-reader user who has just submitted a roster and is waiting is told nothing like "Graph ready — 5 people, quality 100%"; they must independently discover the new content by exploring from the search box.
gating.failure: Drive App() through dispatchGenerate() then transition the mocked worker to status "done": diff every element matching `[aria-live]` before/after — only `.busy-live` changes, and only to the empty string; no region states roster size, quality, or any positive outcome.
gating.remediation: Fold a short result sentence (e.g. reusing `peopleNoun`/`buddiesEachLabel`/`connectionSummary`, already computed for the rail and quality panel) into the same permanently-mounted `.busy-live` region on a successful completion, instead of clearing it to empty text, so the transition itself is announced rather than only inferable from where focus lands next.
gating.invariant: On every transition of generation status into "done" (view becomes non-null from null, or a reroll adopts a new view), at least one already-mounted live region's text must change to a non-empty string describing the outcome, not merely revert to empty.

A screen-reader user who has just submitted a roster and is waiting is told nothing like "Graph ready — 5 people, quality 100%"; they must independently discover the new content by exploring from the search box.
confirmed.failure: Drive App() through dispatchGenerate() then transition the mocked worker to status "done": diff every element matching `[aria-live]` before/after — only `.busy-live` changes, and only to the empty string; no region states roster size, quality, or any positive outcome.
confirmed.remediation: Fold a short result sentence (e.g. reusing `peopleNoun`/`buddiesEachLabel`/`connectionSummary`, already computed for the rail and quality panel) into the same permanently-mounted `.busy-live` region on a successful completion, instead of clearing it to empty text, so the transition itself is announced rather than only inferable from where focus lands next.
confirmed.invariant: On every transition of generation status into "done" (view becomes non-null from null, or a reroll adopts a new view), at least one already-mounted live region's text must change to a non-empty string describing the outcome, not merely revert to empty.

plausible.theme: a file the organizer asked for can silently fail to arrive because the blob URL backing it is torn down in the same task as the click that consumes it
plausible.summary: `downloadBlob` calls `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` synchronously on the line after `a.click()`, on an anchor that is never attached to the document — the two conditions under which a browser can drop the download entirely, silently, with no error to surface.
plausible.failure: Not reproducible under jsdom (which stubs `URL.createObjectURL`/`click`) and not covered by `app/test/download.test.ts`, which exercises only `neutralizeCell`/`toCsv`. Traced statically: `const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob); a.href = url; a.click(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url);` — the click queues the download task, and the revoke runs before that task can read the blob. In engines that fetch the blob asynchronously (this is why MDN's own guidance is to revoke on a later task) Export ↓ and CSV produce no file and no message; both are the organizer's only way to get the roster off the device, and the e2e driver runs Chromium only, where the pattern happens to work. Marked PLAUSIBLE because the failure is engine-dependent and I could not observe it in this environment.
plausible.remediation: Revoke on a later task and attach the anchor before clicking: `document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); a.remove(); setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 0);`. Both spreadsheet-bound sinks and the JSON export already share this one helper, so the fix lands once.
plausible.invariant: An object URL created to back a download is never revoked in the same task as the click that consumes it — i.e. no synchronous `URL.revokeObjectURL` may follow the `click()` that reads it within one turn of the event loop.
